key_claims.claim: More than one-quarter of women with gestational diabetes developed hypertension by five months postpartum, and prenatal factors could predict those at highest risk

Evidence-based synthesis clarifies preoperative cerclage decision-making including indications and timing for history-indicated, ultrasound-indicated, and physical-exam-indicated cerclage in singleton and twin pregnancies
Approximately one-quarter of postpartum women with documented hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were unaware they had received this diagnosis
Diagnosing isolated polyhydramnios using both elevated AFI and elevated MVP rather than either criterion alone better identifies pregnancies at risk for adverse perinatal outcomes
Women with HDP in twin gestations have similar long-term cardiometabolic and cardiovascular morbidity as those with singleton HDP, with comparable recurrence rates in subsequent pregnancies
